data.message: I found Frank's body in medbay. My route was security → weapons → cafeteria → medbay. I didn't see anyone along the way until I walked into medbay and found him dead. That means whoever killed him likely came from one of medbay's other connections — upper engine, electrical, or storage — since I came from cafeteria and saw no one there. I'd like to hear where everyone else was, especially anyone who was near those rooms.

I was working on calibration in electrical for most of the round. I did pop into medbay briefly to check the task board there, but it was empty when I went through — no body, no players. Then I went back to electrical to finish up. So if Frank was killed in medbay, it must have happened after I left. I didn't see anyone else on my path, which honestly worries me because that means the killer was being careful about timing. I'd really like to hear from whoever was in upper engine or storage — those are the other ways into medbay.

My route was short — I started in oxygen, did a bit of work there, then moved to upper engine where I've been since tick 6. Diana was already there when I arrived — actually, she came up from lower engine at tick 6, and we've been together in upper engine since then. So Diana and I can vouch for each other for the back half of the round.

That's important because upper engine is one of the routes into medbay that Alice mentioned. Neither of us went that way — we stayed put together.

That leaves Bob and the storage/electrical angle. Eve says she was in electrical and passed through medbay when it was empty. If that's true, then Bob is the one we haven't heard from yet — and storage connects to medbay too. I want to hear Bob's route before I point fingers, but right now Diana and I clear each other, and Eve's story is at least testable.

Charlie's account matches mine exactly. I started in lower engine, moved up to upper engine at tick 6, and Charlie was already there — we've been together since. Neither of us went toward medbay, so we alibi each other for the back half of the round.

That leaves Bob unaccounted for. Eve says she was in electrical and passed through medbay when it was empty — that's plausible but not verifiable. Alice came from cafeteria and found the body. The killer most likely came from storage or electrical.

I want to hear Bob's route before voting. If Bob can't account for himself near storage or electrical, he's our prime suspect. Otherwise, we need to scrutinize Eve's medbay pass-through more carefully — she's the only one who admits being in the murder room.

My route was simple: I started in navigation and moved to storage. I've been in storage trying to start the Sort Cargo task. I didn't see anyone the entire round — no one passed through navigation while I was there, and storage was empty when I arrived.

Now, I know storage connects to medbay, so I understand why I'm a suspect from Diana and Charlie's perspective. But here's the thing: if I had killed Frank in medbay, I would've had to go medbay → storage, and I'd have nothing to show for my round. I have no witnesses, which is bad for me, but the same is true for Eve — and Eve actually admits to being in the murder room.

Charlie and Diana clearly alibi each other in upper engine. Alice came from cafeteria and saw no one. That leaves me and Eve as the only two who could have done it. Eve placed herself in medbay during the window and is the only person who admits being in the room where Frank died. Her "it was empty when I passed through" is convenient and unverifiable — exactly what a Duck would say to preempt suspicion.

I'm voting Eve. If I'm wrong, I'll be the obvious next target and you'll know. But Eve putting herself in the murder room is the strongest lead we have.

Wait, I think there's some confusion about speaker order — I already gave my report at the start. But since I have the floor again, let me synthesize what we've heard.

Charlie and Diana alibi each other in upper engine from tick 6 onward — that's a solid mutual vouch, though of course if they're both Ducks it falls apart (but we only have one Duck this game, so at most one of them is lying, meaning the other genuinely clears them).

That leaves Bob and Eve as the realistic suspects. Eve admits being in medbay. Bob was in storage — also adjacent to medbay. Both are unverified.

Eve's story has a wrinkle: she says she passed through medbay and it was empty, then went back to electrical. That's a lot of movement for "calibration in electrical for most of the round." Bob's story is simpler — navigation to storage, stayed there.

I'm leaning Eve. Putting yourself in the murder room and claiming it was "empty" is a classic preemptive alibi. I'll vote Eve unless someone gives me a strong reason otherwise.

Okay, I need to push back here because the logic is being twisted against me unfairly.

Yes, I passed through medbay — and I'll add something I didn't mention before: I actually saw Frank in medbay when I passed through. He was alive. I didn't think much of it at the time because he looked like he was about to start a task. If I had killed him, why would I volunteer that I was in the room AND that I saw him there? That's the worst possible lie — I'd just say I never went to medbay at all.

Bob's logic sounds clean but it's backwards. A Duck doesn't admit to being in the murder room unless they're being honest. A Duck says "I was in navigation the whole time, saw nothing" — which is exactly what Bob said. His story is the unverifiable one: no witnesses, no one passed through, conveniently isolated next to medbay via storage.

Think about timing: I saw Frank ALIVE in medbay at one point. Someone came in after me and killed him. Storage connects directly to medbay. Bob admits being in storage the whole time with no witnesses.

Charlie and Diana alibi each other. Alice came from cafeteria. That leaves me and Bob — and Bob had the same access I did, with a cleaner-sounding but equally unverifiable story.

I'm voting Bob.

Diana and I still clear each other in upper engine — that hasn't changed. So this comes down to Bob vs. Eve, and I've been weighing both sides carefully.

Eve's new detail — that she saw Frank alive in medbay — is interesting. It could be honest (placing the kill after her pass-through), or it could be a Duck pre-empting the obvious "you were in the room" accusation by adding verifiable-sounding color. Both readings are plausible.

But here's what tips me: Eve's movement pattern is electrical → medbay → electrical. That's a weird loop unless you had a reason to check medbay. Bob's route is a straight line: navigation → storage, sat down to do a task. Simpler routes are usually more honest, not less — Ducks tend to manufacture activity.

Also, Eve volunteering "I saw Frank alive" only AFTER Bob accused her is suspicious timing. If that were true, she should have led with it in her first speech — it's the single most exculpatory thing she could say. Adding it now reads as adjusting the story under pressure.

I'm leaning Bob's read. I'll vote Eve, but I want to hear if Diana sees it differently before we lock in.

I agree with Charlie's read, and I want to add my own weight to it.

Eve's story shifted under pressure. In her first speech, she said medbay was "empty — no body, no players." Now, after Bob accused her, suddenly she remembers seeing Frank alive in there. Those two statements aren't compatible. "Empty" means empty. Either she lied the first time or she's adjusting now — either way, that's a serious credibility problem.

Bob's story is unverified, yes, but it's consistent and simple. Eve's is unverified AND has changed mid-meeting. That's the bigger red flag.

Charlie and I clear each other in upper engine. Alice came from cafeteria. Between Bob and Eve, Eve put herself in the murder room and then changed her account of what she saw there.

I'm voting Eve.

Thanks Diana — that's exactly the inconsistency I was going to highlight. Eve's first speech was explicit: "it was empty when I went through — no body, no players." Now suddenly she saw Frank alive in there. You don't forget seeing the victim alive in the murder room. That's a story change under pressure, full stop.

To recap where we are: Charlie and Diana mutually alibi each other in upper engine. Alice came from cafeteria and found the body. That leaves me and Eve as the realistic suspects. I was in navigation then storage trying to start Sort Cargo — yes, unverified, but my story hasn't changed once. Eve's has.

The "Bob's simple route is suspicious" argument is backwards. Simple routes aren't suspicious — they're just what doing tasks looks like. Eve's electrical → medbay → electrical loop is the manufactured-activity pattern, and her account of medbay shifted the moment she was pressured.

I'm voting Eve.
